newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen up 5,000T, aluminium down.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen up 5,000T, aluminium down.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks are expected to rise by about 5,000 tonnes while aluminium inventories could dip later on Friday, Singapore-based metal traders said.
"We are expecting a rise of about 5,000 tonnes on copper stocks and aluminium could fall slightly," one trader said.
Earlier, traders in New York were forecasting a copper stocks build of between 5,000 to 8,000 tonnes, largely in the United States with some increases also seen in Singapore and West European stores.
Three month LME zinc, already near a two-year high, is destined for another run-up if LME stocks fall, as expected, by 8,000 tonnes or so, Australian dealers said on Friday.
Zinc is rallying in response to growing sentiment that world supplies of the metal will tighten in the second half of 1997 due to mine closures, they said.

Zinc came under pressure in London on Thursday to settle US$2.00 a tonne lower as profit-takers zoomed in on what was perceived as an overbought market, but not before hefty buying swept the three-month contract to a fresh 23-month high of $1,133 a tonne.
Three month LME aluminium was indicated at $1,607/12 a tonne at 0430 GMT, hardly changed from Thursday's LME kerb close.
"The (LME) market for all metals is likely to trade within a $10-20 range (on Friday). It's going to be a boring day," the trader said.
In Singapore, the quantity of copper held on warrant in the LME warehouse fell to 39,550 tonnes on Tuesday, down 500 tonnes from the previous exchange report on January 10.
Three month LME copper was quoted by regional dealers at around $2,250/55 a tonne at 0430 GMT on Friday, slightly above the LME kerb close of $2,248 on Thursday.
Support for copper was assessed at $2,237.

One trader said he did not expect copper to react "strongly" to any LME stocks movement. He said there had already been an underlying "sell-off" in the red metal in past two days as traders squared positions ahead of an effective three-day -- Ang Bee Lin, Singapore newsroom (65-870-3082)
